  github.com/ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina/runtime.(*Runtime).Init()
issues.edge_case_reason: Ordinary code: a module init starting a strand is a common pattern.
issues.reasoning: Reproduced on main with a -race build of ./cli/cmd using the issue's project (3/3 runs report the race: exec.executeCall reads the function-descriptor map while Registry.RegisterModule writes it from Runtime.Init). BIR is fine; this is a runtime/interpreter concurrency bug, not a spec question, so it is valid as an implementation defect (unsynchronised map access can abort with 'concurrent map read and map write'). Not runtime-crash: no crash observed without -race. Related to #1558 (nightly race detector) but not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: Computed key in a mapping constructor overwrites a readonly record field instead of panicking
issues.edge_case_reason: Needs a computed key that collides with a readonly field set by a specific field in the same constructor.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. BIR is correct (newMap marks [k] as computed); the interpreter's execNewMap only checks the computed value's type against the field type and never checks the field's read-only bit. Clean-context spec check: VALID per §6.7.2 (computed fields applied as modifications; incompatible modification panics) and §5.4.2 (readonly field). No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: join clause rejects a literal on the right of `equals` ("incompatible type: expected 1, got int")
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected 1, got int

issues.edge_case_reason: A literal on one side of a join's `equals` is an unusual way to write a join.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: valid program rejected with a wrong SEMANTIC_ERROR. Clean-context spec check: VALID, §6.35.4 gives no typing rule linking the two `equals` operands, so the program should compile and print [1]. No duplicate (related query-join issues #1047, #1651 are different).

issues.title: [Bug]: a class cannot implement resource methods it includes from an object type
issues.output:
fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: unexpected member kind in object type descriptor
 --> 1800.bal:4:5
issues.edge_case_reason: Object type inclusion of a client object type that declares resource methods is a rarely used construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main with INTERNAL_ERROR (the same symptom as #1294; once #1294/PR #1662 lands the issue reports UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR, so it is a follow-up, not a duplicate). Clean-context spec check: VALID, the program is well formed and should print 'impl'. Related: #1294, #1673 (resource members keyed by accessor+ordinal, root cause per the issue), #1671. Consider making it a sub-issue of #1673.

issues.output:

issues.edge_case_reason: Client resource access through an object type descriptor (not a class) is a less common construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main with INTERNAL_ERROR (same symptom as #1294; after PR #1662 it becomes UNIMPLEMENTED_ERROR plus the #1671 subtyping error, so it is a follow-up, not a duplicate). Consider making it a sub-issue of #1673.

issues.title: [Bug]: chained relational operators (`a < b < c`) are accepted although relational operators are non-associative
issues.edge_case_reason: Chained relational comparison is invalid code that real programs rarely write.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: parser accepts `a < b < b` as left-associative and the program prints false. Clean-context spec check: VALID, the §6 precedence table gives relational operators associativity 'non', so this must be a compile-time error. Frontend (parser). No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: nested member-access lvexpr evaluates the outer key after the inner key (wrong evaluation order)
issues.edge_case_reason: Only observable with side-effecting index expressions in a nested member-access lvexpr.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. The dumped BIR calls f("outer") and does the filling read before calling f("inner"), so the BIR is wrong for the source -> frontend (BIR gen). Clean-context spec check: VALID per §7.15.1 (index expression evaluated before the sub-lvexpr) and §7.15.2. Related to #1634 (rvalue order) and #1217 (compound assignment), not duplicates.

notes: All 7 new issues reproduce on main 1bcb85b9e and were confirmed valid by a clean-context spec check (#1815 is a Go-level data race, validated as an implementation defect instead). All already have Type/Bug. #1799 and #1800 hit INTERNAL_ERROR on main (the #1294 symptom), so frontend_internal_error is true; they remain distinct follow-ups to #1294 and may belong under #1673. No frontend crashes (Go panics). Skipped issues were in earlier reports with no updates since.
